title: An Alien Spaceship? Strange 8-Foot Crater Found On UK Farm After Mysterious Light Appeared In The Sky In 1963 - What Did The British Army Find On The Land?
excerpt: UK UFO Sightings: Did a UFO land on a British farm in 1963? A mysterious crater, strange orange light and unexplained marks baffled investigators as the Charlton UFO mystery continues.
content:
UK UFO Sightings: A strange orange light streaking across the sky, a loud bang in the early morning and a mysterious crater appearing in a farmer’s field – the events reported in a small British village in July 1963 sound like something straight out of a science-fiction film. But this was no movie scene. The discovery at Roy Blanchard’s farm in Charlton, Wiltshire, attracted police officers, military personnel, scientists and UFO investigators.

Even after the Army examined the site, nobody established exactly what had created the unusual formation. More than six decades later, the Charlton Crater remains one of Britain’s most talked-about UFO mysteries.

UFO Sightings: Strange Orange Light Spotted Before Mysterious Crater Appeared

The mystery began in July 1963 when a policeman reportedly spotted an unusual streak of orange light in the sky above Charlton, Wiltshire.

Around the same period, Leonard ‘Len’ Joliffe, a worker at Manor Farm, heard what he described as a massive bang while travelling to work early in the morning. He worked as a milkman for farmer Roy Blanchard.

His brother, Gordon Joliffe, later recalled the incident in the 2004 documentary The British UFO Files.

‘He was on his way to work at 6 o’clock in the morning because he was a milker; he worked for Mr Blanchard,’ Gordon explained. Len was reportedly on his bike when he heard ‘this great big bang in the morning, after the huge light in the sky came down’.

But the biggest shock came when another farmworker, Reginald Alexander, discovered something unusual in the field.

He found a huge crater in an area where the farm usually grew potatoes and barley. He immediately informed Blanchard, and the discovery soon attracted attention from journalists, investigators and military experts.

UFO Sightings: What Did The Mysterious Charlton Crater Look Like?

The formation was unlike an ordinary hole in the ground. Its unusual design became one of the biggest reasons the incident attracted attention.

UFO researcher Waveney Girvan documented the discovery in the autumn 1963 edition of Flying Saucer Review. He described the main depression as eight feet in diameter and around four inches deep.

At its centre, investigators found a hole approximately three feet deep. Four long, narrow marks extended from the central hole, creating a pattern that looked like the spokes of a giant wheel.

Even more strangely, reports described the affected area as bare, despite the surrounding land being used to grow potatoes and barley.

The unusual formation raised an obvious question: What could have created such a pattern without leaving the signs of a conventional impact?

UFO Sightings: Army Bomb Disposal Team Arrives To Investigate UFO Mystery

The discovery prompted concerns that an unexploded World War II bomb might have remained buried beneath the farmland.

Given Britain’s wartime history, investigators could not ignore the possibility of an old explosive device. The Army therefore sent a bomb disposal team to examine the crater.

However, the team did not find an unexploded bomb or evidence that an explosion had taken place at the site.

The investigation also became a subject of discussion in the British Parliament. On August 1, 1963, Secretary of State for War Joseph Godber addressed the matter in the House of Commons.

He said: “The Army was concerned only to discover whether the crater could contain an unexploded bomb. Nothing of this nature was found and the Bomb Disposal Unit left the site on Friday, 26th July.”

The Army’s findings ruled out one major possibility but did not explain how the strange formation had appeared.

UFO Sightings: Meteorite Theory Also Failed To Explain The Strange Discovery

Could a meteorite have crashed into the field? Astronomer Patrick Moore reportedly supported this explanation.

Investigators had discovered a metallic-looking piece of material at the site, which initially appeared to offer a possible clue.

However, the British Museum examined the sample and identified it as ordinary ironstone, a material commonly found in the Wiltshire region.

This discovery weakened the meteorite theory and left the mystery unresolved.

UFO Sightings: Farmer Roy Blanchard Believed A Spaceship Had Visited His Farm

While investigators struggled to find an explanation, the farmer himself had a rather extraordinary theory.

Roy Blanchard believed that something powerful had landed on his property but had done so without producing the usual signs of an explosion.

He reflected: ‘The thing was heavy enough to crush rocks and stone to powder. Yet it came down gently. We heard no crash and whatever power it uses produces no heat or noise. I believe that we have received a visit from a spaceship from another world.’

His comments became one of the most memorable parts of the Charlton Crater story and fuelled speculation about a possible extraterrestrial encounter.

However, his belief was not backed by verified evidence of an alien spacecraft.

UFO Sightings: Is The 1963 Charlton Crater Mystery Still Unsolved?

More than 60 years after the discovery, the Charlton Crater continues to feature in discussions about Britain’s unexplained UFO incidents.

The Army found no unexploded bomb, while the metallic sample did not establish a meteorite impact. The Air Ministry also did not consider the incident serious enough to warrant further investigation.

That left UFO enthusiasts with plenty of questions but no confirmed answer.

Did an unidentified object really land on the farm, or was the crater caused by something far more ordinary that investigators failed to identify? The available evidence does not settle the question, keeping the 1963 Charlton Crater among Britain’s enduring unexplained mysteries.
